sources.note: Bare wordlist, no prose beyond a two-line header ('from a manuscript by Galis (1956)'; 'Due to the poor printing quality of the manuscript, the transcriptions need to be double-checked'); no transcription key, no remark on stress, accent or tone. Of the 94 Doeboe forms, 15 carry an acute accent (wéjalgi 'boom', djalé 'baik', singkěré 'drie', né 'echtgenote', tongkwár 'mens', kléseri 'mond', tambó 'nieuw', piáii 'rood', klé 'tand', klémalbb 'tong', kré 'twee', wé 'vuur', froek-wár 'vliegen', nafo-fakléi 'warm', aléikio 'zien') and many carry ě (schwa); since é also sits on monosyllables (klé,…

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2024 (page last modified 2024-06-25). Tebi-Towe. NewGuineaWorld, Santa Fe Institute.https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/pauwasi-river/west-pauwasi-river/tebi-towe/start
sources.note: No statement about stress placement. Historical-phonology page (under construction) reconstructs Proto-Tebi-Towe consonants and vowels; its comparative tables reproduce Im's (2005) Tebi transcriptions with primary-stress marks (e.g. ˈmi 'louse', muˈmi 'mosquito', minˈdi 'nose', nuˈmu '1pl', piˈsi 'tree kangaroo', teˈpa 'forest'), i.e. raw data with stress on varying syllables, no rule given. The page is also the fullest inventory of Dubu/Tebi sources: Anceaux (Smits & Voorhoeve 1994: 104 terms, Afi and Dubu villages, collectors Walton and D. A. Mallo), Galis 1956: 85-97, Voorhoeve 1971: 98-10…

sources.note: No phonology content for Tebi; documentation-status survey. Notes that extensive materials exist only for the related Karkar-Yuri [yuj] (Price 1987 etc.), a different languoid.

sources.citation: Whitehouse, Paul. 2006. The 'Lost' Paper: A Belated Conference Postscript. Mother Tongue (Journal of the Association for the Study of Language in Prehistory) XI: 262-274. [section 'A New Grouping in Central New Guinea?' with Pauwasi/Kehu/Trans-Fly lexical comparisons; archive.org item mother-tongue-xi-2006]
sources.note: No phonology; isolated Dubu lexical forms in etymological sets only (wordlist-level data, no prosodic marking). The words stress/tone/accent do not occur in the article.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-459. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: Australian National University. [sec. 2.6.2.2.13 'The Pauwasi Stock', pp. 418-419]
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for any Pauwasi language; the section is classification + demography and states that only wordlists exist. (The chapter does give sound-system notes for some other stocks, e.g. Morwap, but not Pauwasi.)

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 108 DUBU (Pauwasi Stock, Western Family; villages Dubu, Wenk, Yambe, Afi; c. 130 speakers; sources Galis 1956b, Voorhoeve 1971) plus a 40-item comparative wordlist in a unified orthography described as 'neither phonemic nor accurately phonetic'. No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole volume.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In T. Dutton et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 47-114. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6 'The Pauwasi Phylum' (p. 77) says the only Dubu data are Galis's 1956b wordlists, which 'do not allow conclusions about phonological and grammatical structure'; Appendix I (pp. 98-109) gives an 84-item Dubu wordlist after Galis with no stress marks. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in the Dubu material; the only pitch/tone remarks in the paper concern Sko and Sawuj, not Dubu.
